14.0.0.en: These verses were explained in (2 Sam 5:11, 12), and in them we see how God established David's kingdom: Hiram king of Tyre, which was one of the great cities at that time, sent to bless him on his reign, and he presented him with many gifts.

14.0.1.en: If you please God with your love, your repentance and your good works, God will bless you and give you favor in the eyes of those around you, that you may grow in love for Him and in the love of all.

14.0.2.en: (2) The sons of David in Jerusalem (vv. 3 - 7:)-

14.0.3.en: 3- And David took more wives at Jerusalem: and David begat more sons and daughters. 4- Now these are the names of his children which he had in Jerusalem; Shammua, and Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, 5- And Ibhar, and Elishua, and Elpalet, 6- And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia, 7- And Elishama, and Beeliada, and Eliphalet.

14.0.4.en: We explained these verses in (2 Sam 5:13-16), and in them we see God's blessing on David in the many sons and daughters born to him in Jerusalem. He is a type of Christ, who has many sons and daughters who have believed in Him in the whole world.

14.0.5.en: Be careful to adorn yourself with the virtues, which are counted as sons and daughters to you, so that through them you may sense God in your life and by them be made worthy to enter the Kingdom of Heaven. The closer you cling to God, the more virtues He bestows on you.

15.0.0.en: These events were mentioned briefly in (2 Sam 6:12, 13). What happened was that David understood his error in the way he moved the ark and his violation of the Law, since the priests did not carry it but they placed it on a cart. Therefore the oxen rushed forward and Uzza died, and he offered repentance to God, especially after he saw God's blessing on the house of Obed-edom because of the presence of the ark with him.

15.0.1.en: So David prepared a tent in Jerusalem, after he had built houses for himself and for the administration of the kingdom, and this tent was to receive the ark. As for the tabernacle of meeting, with its remaining parts, it was in the city of Gibeon. Abiathar, the second high priest, was in Jerusalem to serve the ark, and this arrangement was temporary and ended in the days of Solomon, after the building of the Temple, when Zadok alone became the high priest for the service of the Temple in Jerusalem. David gathered all the people of Israel who were concerned for the worship of God in Jerusalem and declared to them what the Law prescribes, which is that the ark of the covenant of God may be carried by no one but the priests only. This shows David's humility, since he declared his error of the first time before all the people, so that everyone would be bound by the Law of God.

15.0.2.en: Be strong enough to apologize for your error, and do not justify yourself or try to cover the sin, because God rejoices in His repentant children, and people also will respect you for your frankness and humility, and by this, without knowing it, you teach them true humility.

15.1.0.en: David gathered a great number of priests and Levites, eight hundred and sixty-two, under the leadership of six chiefs, to carry out the service of the ark. This shows his concern to involve everyone in the service so that they might receive its blessing, and his great concern for the service of God, so that he gathered for Him all this huge number.

15.2.0.en: After David gathered the high priests Zadok and Abiathar and all the chiefs, the priests and the Levites, he declared to them that their sin in not carrying the ark, and being content to place it on a cart, was the reason for God's anger. He also declared to them the necessity of preparing themselves by purifying themselves to carry out this great service, which was the moving of the ark of the covenant of God. Then he added the necessity of their commitment that the priests carry the ark with poles, as the Law prescribes, that is, as God decreed. The rest of the Levites were to help them. So everyone obeyed and purified themselves and carried the ark from the house of Obed-edom.

15.2.1.en: The Second Book of Samuel tells us how greatly David honored the ark, in the sacrifices he offered before the ark throughout its journey from the house of Obed-edom to Jerusalem.

15.2.3.en: 16- And David spake to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brethren to be the singers with instruments of musick, psalteries and harps and cymbals, sounding, by lifting up the voice with joy. 17- So the Levites appointed Heman the son of Joel; and of his brethren, Asaph the son of Berechiah; and of the sons of Merari their brethren, Ethan the son of Kushaiah; 18- And with them their brethren of the second degree, Zechariah, Ben, and Jaaziel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Unni, Eliab, and Benaiah, and Maaseiah, and Mattithiah, and Elipheleh, and Mikneiah, and Obededom, and Jeiel, the porters.

15.2.4.en: 19- So the singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, were appointed to sound with cymbals of brass; 20- And Zechariah, and Aziel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Unni, and Eliab, and Maaseiah, and Benaiah, with psalteries on Alamoth; 21- And Mattithiah, and Elipheleh, and Mikneiah, and Obededom, and Jeiel, and Azaziah, with harps on the Sheminith to excel. 22- And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was for song: he instructed about the song, because he was skilful. 23- And Berechiah and Elkanah were doorkeepers for the ark. 24- And Shebaniah, and Jehoshaphat, and Nethaneel, and Amasai, and Zechariah, and Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, did blow with the trumpets before the ark of God: and Obededom and Jehiah were doorkeepers for the ark.

15.3.0.en: Harps: plural of the lute ('ud), an ancient musical instrument, which still exists to this day. It is a box with strings on it.

15.3.1.en: Psalteries: a small ancient stringed instrument, over which usually a single string is stretched.

15.3.2.en: Cymbals: plural of cymbal, and they are the cymbals used in our churches now. They are made of brass, and when they touch they produce sounds that regulate and lead the hymns and praises.

15.3.3.en: David was also concerned to present spiritual songs before the ark, in honor of God. So David asked the chiefs of the Levites to gather the singers and give them musical instruments, such as harps, psalteries and cymbals, so that the songs would be accompanied by suitable music.

15.4.0.en: David chose three of the singers, distinguished in leadership, namely Asaph, with Heman and Ethan, and made them chiefs over the singers.

15.5.0.en: Of the second degree: the assistants, that is, those who are in the second rank after the leaders.

15.5.1.en: He also chose fourteen men of the singers, distinguished ones, to be assistants to the three chiefs of the singers mentioned above.

15.5.2.en: We notice that these assistants in leading the singers were at the same time doorkeepers, that is, responsible for guarding the ark.

15.5.3.en: 19-21: Leading the singers. David divided the work in organizing the singing, and David gave these responsibilities:-

15.5.4.en: 1- The leadership, as we mentioned, was given to Asaph, Heman and Ethan, to lead the singers by means of the cymbals, just as happens now, when the head deacon leads the rest of the deacons and the people, using the cymbals.

15.5.5.en: 2- He assigned six of the singers to use the psalteries, to present a high register of the voice, called the "jawab" (the upper register), which in the Jesuit translation is "the melody of the maidens," and which corresponds now to the range called "Tenor."

15.5.6.en: 3- He also chose six of the singers to sing in a low register called the "qarar" (the lower register), so these six lead this voice, which corresponds now to the Basses, and they lead it with the harps.

15.6.0.en: - David chose a chief from the Levites whose responsibility was the carrying, or the moving, that is, he was responsible for carrying the ark and moving it.

15.7.0.en: - David also chose from the Levites two groups, each of which carried out a particular responsibility, namely:-

15.7.1.en: 1- The doorkeepers of the ark, that is, those responsible for guarding it while it was being moved, or after it was placed in the tent. He assigned four persons here to carry out this responsibility.

15.7.2.en: 2- David chose seven of the priests for the responsibility of blowing the trumpets before the ark. The trumpet is a musical instrument with a loud sound, made of bronze or silver, and it gives honor and majesty to the ark and alerts the people to stand, or to bow down, and to honor the ark.

15.7.3.en: How great David was in his concern for the ark and his honoring of it! And you, are you concerned to honor God in the Church, by coming early and concentrating in the prayers, so that you may enjoy the sense of Him and rejoice in Him?

15.7.5.en: 25- So David, and the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands, went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the house of Obededom with joy. 26- And it came to pass, when God helped the Levites that bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, that they offered seven bullocks and seven rams. 27- And David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, and all the Levites that bare the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the master of the song with the singers: David also had upon him an ephod of linen. 28- Thus all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the Lord with shouting, and with sound of the cornet, and with trumpets, and with cymbals, making a noise with psalteries and harps.

15.7.6.en: 29- And it came to pass, as the ark of the covenant of the Lord came to the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looking out at a window saw king David dancing and playing: and she despised him in her heart. This subject was mentioned with other details in (2 Sam 6:12 - 16)

15.8.0.en: Here he specifies those who went to bring up the ark from the house of Obed-edom, namely King David, the elders of the people and the captains of thousands, that is, all the leaders of the people. Of course a great number of the people followed them, and they were filled with joy, since the blessing of the Lord had been shown to the house of Obed-edom when the ark was with him for three months (ch. 13:14).

15.8.1.en: When you see God's blessing on His saints and His children in every generation, follow their example, walk with God as they did, and strive in the way of their virtues, and you also will receive a blessing from God, and by this, without feeling it, you will become a light to the world and draw many to God.

15.9.0.en: - The fear of God was upon the hearts of the priests and the Levites, who were charged with carrying the ark of the covenant and walking behind it, because of the death of Uzza. Therefore the grace of God intervened to help them and reassure them as they carried the ark. Here we find joy mingled with fear, which made them offer seven bullocks and seven rams, in addition to sacrificing an ox and a fatling whenever the priests who bore the ark had gone six paces (2 Sam 6:13).

15.10.0.en: (David took off his great royal garments and put on, like the priests, garments of linen. This was humility on David's part, and at the same time it represented his sanctification of the ark. The clothes that David wore were an ephod and a robe, which are two garments, one of which reaches to the feet and the other is shorter than it. The high priest used to wear them, and in special cases other persons wore them, such as Samuel (1 Sam 2:18). David here is a type of Christ the King, Priest and Prophet, since each of them wore linen.

15.11.0.en: Cornets: plural of sur, a trumpet made from the horn of an animal.

15.11.1.en: The people walked with the priests who bore the ark, the king, the elders and the chiefs, and they shouted with great joy, and they used various musical instruments, such as psalteries and harps and loud-sounding instruments such as trumpets.

15.12.0.en: The procession of the ark reached the city of David, which is a part of Jerusalem, and everyone was shouting with joy, and with them the king, who was dancing before the ark with all his might, because he was in great joy. When his wife Michal, the daughter of Saul, looked out from the window of her house, she saw David dancing, wearing linen garments, having taken off his royal clothes, and she despised him. This shows her weak esteem for the greatness of God and the holiness of the ark; therefore David rebuked her afterward.

15.12.1.en: David's praise and the service of the ark

16.0.s.en: (1) The burnt offerings and the praise before the ark

16.0.0.en: These verses were mentioned in (2 Sam 6:17-19). A question may arise: why did David not bring the tabernacle and what was in it from Gibeon to Jerusalem to place the ark in it, but set up a special tent in Jerusalem in which he placed the ark? The reason, as we think, is that David intended to establish a permanent temple for God in Jerusalem in which to place the ark, but God told him that his son was the one who would build the Temple and not he. The tabernacle had been at Shiloh, as we mentioned, and in it the ark (ch. 13:3); then after the Philistines took the ark, the tabernacle was moved to Nob (1 Sam 21:1-9), and after Saul killed the priests at Nob (1 Sam 22:17-19) the tabernacle was moved to Gibeon (ch. 16:39, ch. 21:29). Thus David finally achieved what his heart longed for and declared in Psalm (132:3, 4), that his heart would not rest, nor settle in his house, nor would he give sleep to his eyes, until he found a place for the Lord. This was fulfilled when he placed the ark of the covenant in a tent in Jerusalem, to offer to Him holy service and worship.

16.1.0.en: To record: to remember God's benefits and thank Him for them.

16.1.1.en: Here the book adds David's arrangement of the service of praise before the ark of the covenant of God, and shows that the leader of the singers was Asaph, and with him a great number of Levites and also the priests, and they had the musical instruments, to glorify God in groups and in a fixed order. David had prepared a song for this occasion, which he gave to Asaph and the singers to repeat with music before the ark, and we shall explain this song in the following verses.

16.1.2.en: Asaph wrote twelve psalms within the Book of Psalms, and he took care to teach his sons praise, so that one hundred and twenty-eight of his descendants returned from the captivity trained in praise (Ezra 2:41), and they praised at the renewal of the Temple in the days of Ezra the priest (Ezra 3:10). Thus David offered two things to the ark of God:

16.1.5.en: It is noted that the number of chiefs of the singers mentioned in (vv. 5, 6) is smaller than those mentioned in (ch. 15), because some of the singers were before the ark in Jerusalem under the leadership of Asaph, and another group of the singers were under the leadership of Heman and Jeduthun before the tabernacle in Gibeon (vv. 41, 42).

16.1.6.en: If you love God, you will spontaneously wish to praise Him, to rejoice His heart and rejoice with Him. So be careful to take part in the Midnight Praise (Tasbeha) in the Church, that you may become accustomed to it and love it and enjoy it also in your private room.

16.2.0.en: David calls the people to thank God and to mention His name and His benefits, so that it may spread among the nations and they may believe in God. That is, he asks three things of the people: thanksgiving, prayer and preaching, as he says (give thanks, call upon, make known).

16.3.0.en: David asks the people to be concerned for praise, in saying "sing" and "sing psalms," and also that the conversations of the people with one another be filled with talk about the wondrous works of God with them, so that they may live a life of thanksgiving.

16.4.0.en: David shows the blessings of praise, since it gives the one who praises:

16.4.1.en: 1- Boasting and confidence in the soul that trusts in God.

16.4.2.en: 2- Joy and consolation that cannot be expressed.

16.5.0.en: When a person discovers, through praise, the greatness of God, he seeks His help and His strength (His might), and even seeks Him continually, so that he comes to trust in Him at all times and enters into what is called the life of prayer.

16.6.0.en: It shows the importance of repeating the works of God (His marvellous works) and thanking Him for them, in addition to His commandments and His Law (the judgments of His mouth), for repeating the word of God establishes it in the heart and influences a person's conduct, so that he lives for God.

16.7.0.en: He rejoices the hearts of the people of God, who are the descendants of Jacob Israel, with the truth that God is our God, that is, we are His own and His chosen, and this gives them reassurance and strength, because He is the Ruler of all (His judgments are in all the earth).

16.8.0.en: David directs them to remember the promises of God that He gave to their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, which are promises of blessing for their descendants if they keep His commandments, that is, David warns them to keep the commandments of God so that they may enjoy His covenants.

16.8.1.en: By "a thousand generations" he means the continuation of God's covenants forever. Heaven and earth will pass away, but the word of God will not pass away, and the steadfastness of God's promises calls us to praise Him continually.

16.9.0.en: The cord of your inheritance: lands were measured with ropes of a certain length, and what is meant here is the land of Canaan, which God gave as an inheritance to His people; He measured it and knew its area and granted it to them. David reminds his people of the fulfillment of God's promises, which were fulfilled in them, for they were few in number in the days of Jacob, to whom God promised the inheritance of the land of Canaan. This was indeed fulfilled, when God brought His people out of Egypt and they crossed the wilderness of Sinai, then entered and possessed the land of Canaan after hundreds of years. They were seventy men in the days of Jacob, and they entered the land of Canaan numbering approximately two million.

16.9.1.en: Trust in God's promises to you, however weak you may seem and however limited your resources, for He is able to bless you and to work miracles in you, and after this do not forget to thank Him always.

16.10.0.en: The people of God, a small number, represented in the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, moved from nation to nation, namely Egypt and Gerar, and God kept them while they were in these kingdoms, so that no one could wrong them. Indeed God rebuked Pharaoh of Egypt (Gen 12:17) when he took Sarah, and likewise Abimelech king of Gerar (Gen 20:3), whom God rebuked in a dream because he had taken Sarah to marry her. This was despite the weakness of the fathers before the power of these kings, but their mighty God kept them and defended them, so these kings sought the blessing of the fathers.

16.11.0.en: Here God declares His keeping of His children and His prevention of the world from hindering His children from their service. "The anointed ones" is the plural of "anointed" (messiah), meaning one anointed with oil, but the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were set apart for God, and they alone believed in Him in the midst of the world, so they were like the anointed. The fathers were not prophets, that is, they did not speak prophecies, but they proclaimed the voice of God by their lives in the world, as the prophets proclaim the voice of God by their prophecies.

16.12.0.en: Here begins the part taken from (Ps 96), in which he calls the whole world, and not only the people of God, to praise Him, and he demands that those who believe in God preach Him among all the nations, because Christ will come to die for the whole world.

16.12.1.en: He asks that the preaching be "from day to day," that is, that it continue in the Old Testament and the New Testament and throughout the generations, so that the nations may see God in those who believe in Him.

16.13.0.en: David demands of the believers that they proclaim God's benefits and His wondrous works in the universe, to alert all the nations and peoples, that they may return to God. And when the world sees the prayers and praises of the believers, how strong and fervent they are, they will believe in their great God, because of the sincerity of their feelings.

16.14.0.en: Why do the believers glorify God? Because God is different from all the pagan gods; He is greater than all gods, glorious (praised) and to be feared, that is, feared by all, because all authority is in His hand. The heavenly beings fear Him, and consequently the earthly beings must glorify Him and fear Him.

16.15.0.en: On the other hand, all the pagan gods are statues of idols that neither speak nor feel; rather, they are tools in the hand of Satan. But God is the true living One, who made the heavens and the earth and all that is in them.

16.16.0.en: In God is perfect purity and beauty, so His presence, that is, His place, rises above every thought in its greatness. Before Him shine His majesty and His blessing, which are shown in His angels and His saints who surround Him. And the strength of God, that is, His power, is in mercy and love for mankind; therefore it gladdens and delights the hearts of His children.

16.17.0.en: Give: bestow a gift, that is, offer a donation and a gift to God.

16.17.1.en: David calls all the nations to submit to God and offer Him gifts and offerings, in glorification of His greatness, and for their worship to be in purity and cleanness of heart, and this is the holy adornment. These offerings are considered praise and thanksgiving to God, the Creator of all and their Provider, who does good to all peoples (Heb 13:15, 16).

16.18.0.en: David calls all mankind to fear God, so that they may behave well and no one wrong another, and so live in stability and peace, and the whole world be established in tranquility, and the devil be unable to create disturbances and divisions, by his stirring up evil desires in hearts.

16.19.0.en: If people fear God, they can then share with the heavenly beings in seeing God and glorifying Him, and so they rejoice, and God reigns over their hearts as He reigns over the heavenly beings, and they come to true happiness.

16.20.0.en: Roar: the waves of the sea crash with force and make a terrifying sound.

16.20.1.en: The sea is a symbol of the world, which is always troubled and disturbed, but it does not affect the children of God, who are settled in His fear, because with God they are stronger than the world, and indeed He subjects the world to them. And the wilderness, which is the barren, deserted land, let it rejoice, because God populates it with solitary monks, who have lived in it from the days of Elijah in the Old Testament until today.

16.21.0.en: The wood: deserted places, in which wild trees grow that bear no fruit.

16.21.1.en: David continues his sense of the submission of all creatures and their joy in God, who reigns over them, and that His coming is near, to judge the evil that is in the world and remove it. The trees of the wood are a symbol of the Gentiles who were without fruit, but when they believe in Christ the Redeemer and submit to Him, they become His children and bear fruit and rejoice at His coming, to judge the evil in the world and raise them with Him to the Kingdom.

16.22.0.en: David ends this part of the song with the praise of God, because He is good; indeed He alone is perfectly good in this world, and He deserves praise and glorification forever.

16.23.0.en: David speaks, in the spirit of prophecy, about the people of God who will be scattered in captivity, and he asks God to save them and bring them back to their land to worship Him in His Temple, and to rescue them from the hands of the nations, that they may live praising and glorifying His great person, and this is their essential work.

16.24.0.en: David concludes his song, blessing God and calling all the people to join in prayer and glorification of Him, as He is blessed and glorified from eternity and to eternity. The people responded to David's call and said "Amen," declaring their agreement with all that Asaph and the singers with him had uttered, and indeed they all joined in the praise of God, that is, the whole people sang a hymn that they knew.

16.25.s.en: (3) The guarding and service of the ark and the tabernacle

16.25.0.en: David's song, which the singers chanted under the leadership of Asaph, was the introduction to an order that David established for offering praises daily before the ark in Jerusalem. By this God's place was restored in His holy city, Jerusalem, and the hearts of the people returned to Him, that He might be their God in all their steps, and that they might glorify Him and seek Him in all their needs.

16.25.1.en: If David organized praises daily before God in the Old Testament, how much more ought praises to be offered today in the Church, at every time, so that we may share with the heavenly beings who praise continually.

16.25.2.en: May you taste the praise of God every day, even with a short hymn, that you may enjoy fellowship with Him, and your heart rejoice and rejoice His heart.

16.26.0.en: David also appointed doorkeepers to guard the ark. It is mentioned that their number was sixty-eight, and they were under the leadership of Obed-edom and his eight brothers, in addition to another person also called Obed-edom, and his companion Hosah. From this David's concern for the ark of the covenant of God appears, as he organized everything pertaining to its service.

16.27.0.en: Gibeon: a city lying northwest of Jerusalem at a distance of five miles.

16.27.1.en: On the other hand, David was concerned for the service of God before the tabernacle of meeting, which was in the city of Gibeon, with all its parts except the ark of the covenant of God, and the city of Gibeon was built on a high place. David arranged that Zadok the high priest and his brothers the priests should be responsible for the service at Gibeon, while Abiathar, the high priest, was responsible for the service in Jerusalem. This was a temporary arrangement in the days of David, that is, the existence of two high priests, but in the days of Solomon Zadok alone became high priest.

16.28.0.en: Zadok and all the priests were concerned to fulfill the Law and to offer the morning and evening burnt offering every day, to declare their love for God and their attachment to Him.

16.28.1.en: Be concerned to pray every day, morning and evening, so that you begin your day and end it with God. Force yourself at the beginning, so that you become accustomed to prayer, and then you will move to the stage of delight and enjoyment of God, and your sense of His presence with you, and His blessings in your life, as you become a son who is near to Him. Open your heart and speak to Him as a son. Thank Him for His benefits and confess your sins before Him, then ask of Him what you want for yourself and for others.

16.29.0.en: Here we find David's concern to arrange the service of praise before the tabernacle of meeting also, so the singers under the leadership of Heman and Jeduthun stand for continual praise, as Asaph leads the praise before the ark of the covenant in Jerusalem, because David felt that the mercies of the Lord are upon His people forever, and so He ought to be thanked at all times for this.

16.29.1.en: The singers used musical instruments with the praises; these instruments were trumpets, cymbals and various other instruments.

16.29.2.en: David was also concerned to guard the tabernacle, so he appointed doorkeepers under the leadership of Jeduthun.

16.30.0.en: After the celebration of placing the ark in Jerusalem was over, and the service for it was arranged, as well as the service of the tabernacle at Gibeon, the people departed, each to his house, and David also, to complete the prayer and the praise of God in their houses. This shows the importance of family prayer in the home, for it is the natural extension of the congregational prayer with the rest of the people in the Church, because a person's love for God in the Church must be accompanied by prayer at home, and family prayer confirms the family's bond and its unity in the love of God. This book did not mention the sin of Michal, David's wife, and her contempt for him when he danced before the ark (2 Sam 6:16), because the book here concentrates on David's love for God and how he is a type of Christ.

16.30.1.en: God's view on the building of His house
